chunks: Humayr ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, and others, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Al-Fadl ibn Abdul Malik, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a woman who inherited her husband, so she emancipated him. Would they remain upon their first marriage? He said: No, but they must renew their marriage.
ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage contract when a wife emancipates her slave-husband after inheriting him?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal status of a marriage between a free woman and her slave-husband when she inherits and emancipates him. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the original marriage contract does not automatically persist post-emancipation, requiring a new contract (ijad al-nikah) to formalize their union. This ruling highlights the distinct legal categories of 'free' and 'slave' in early Islamic jurisprudence, where the change in the husband's status necessitates a renewal of the marital bond to ensure validity.

en.hubeali: Humeyr Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sama’at, from Ja’far Bin Sama’at, and someone else, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Fazl Bin Abdul Malik who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a woman who inherited her husband (a slave), so she emancipated him. Would they both happen to be upon their first marriage?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, but they would both be renewing their marriage’.
